To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) a hybrid system that combines rule-based machine with statistical translation can be used to translate between distantly related languages; (ii) a hybrid system outperforms its individual components; (iii) the hybrid system is more robust than the rule-based system and more fluent than the statistical system; and (iv) a human evaluation of the translation quality shows that humans tend to prefer rule-based machine translations over statistical machine translations.

(i) a hybrid system combining rule-based machine translation with phrase-based statistical translation is better than either of its individual components, (ii) the rule-based translation system performs better than the statistical system according to human evaluation, and (iii) the rule-based system is better at handling long sentences.

a) the hybrid system is the best performing translation system, both automatically and manually; b) the manual evaluation results do not always agree with the automatic evaluation; and c) the hybrid system performs well even if it does not have access to the best possible parse trees.

the development of a hybrid machine translation architecture for the translation of a pair of distanly related languages.

the development of a hybrid architecture for machine translation, which combines the advantages of RBMT and SMT, and is able to produce translations which are more fluent than those from either individual system.
the development of an efficient hybrid machine translation system which is able to take advantage of both rule-based and statistical translation models.

the combination of RBMT with SMT is a promising approach to improve translation quality.
